mainTopic: How the עולת העוף (bird burnt offering) is brought: what it learns from other offerings, and how its מליקה (pinching) is done
overview: A ברייתא works out the rules for the עולת העוף, the bird burnt offering. First it compares it to an animal חטאת. Like that offering, the bird must come from חולין, be brought by day, and be done with the כהן's right hand. Then it stops the comparison from going too far. An animal is valid with most of two סימנים cut, but the bird's head must be fully separated, which is learned from 'ומלק והקטיר'. Next, רבי ישמעאל learns from 'כמשפט' that the עולת העוף is pinched at the back of the neck, like the חטאת העוף. The חטאת העוף leaves one סימן uncut, but 'והקריבו' teaches that the עולת העוף does not. Finally, רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון begins his own reading of 'כמשפט' as pointing to the חטאת העוף, and his comparison continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Bird burnt offering follows the basic rules of an animal sin offering
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא finishes its comparison: like an animal חטאת, the עולת העוף comes only from חולין, by day, and with the right hand.
steps.simpleTranslation: Just as an animal sin offering comes only from non-sacred animals, by day, and with the priest's right hand, so too a bird burnt offering comes only from non-sacred animals, by day, and with the priest's right hand.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא is finishing a comparison that started on the previous page. It applies three rules of the animal חטאת to the עולת העוף.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Three rules carry over to the bird: it must be bought with ordinary money and not מעשר שני money, the service must be done by day, and the כהן must use his right hand. The next steps will test how far this comparison can go.

keyTerms.meaning: Non-sacred, ordinary property (not bought with מעשר שני money)
A burnt offering of a bird
By day; the service is valid only in daytime
His right hand; the כהן must use his right hand

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא מִן הַחוּלִּין, וּבַיּוֹם, וּבְיָדוֹ הַיְמָנִית,
phrases.english: only from non-sacred animals, and by day, and with his right hand,
so too a bird burnt offering comes

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא מִן הַחוּלִּין וּבַיּוֹם וּבְיָדוֹ הַיְמָנִית.
phrases.english: only from non-sacred animals, by day, and with his right hand.

steps.triggerLanguage: אף עולת העוף אינה באה אלא מן החולין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes a comparison that began before this section
steps.mimraCoreRuling: עולת העוף comes only from חולין, is brought by day, and is done with the right hand, like an animal חטאת.

steps.title: Should the bird also be valid with most of two signs cut?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא asks whether the comparison means the bird, like an animal, is valid once most of both סימנים are cut.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, then just as there (an animal sin offering) is valid with most of the two סימנים cut, so too here (the bird burnt offering) should be valid with most of the two סימנים cut?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא pushes the comparison one step further to test it. If the bird is like the animal, maybe cutting most of both סימנים should be enough here too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An animal's שחיטה is valid when most of the windpipe and most of the gullet are cut. The question is whether this rule also carries over to the bird's מליקה. This sets up the answer in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: If so, just as there; a way of asking whether a comparison goes even further
Most of the two סימנים (the windpipe and the gullet)

phrases.english: If so, just as there it is valid with most of the two,
phrases.notes: 'There' is the animal sin offering. 'The two' are the windpipe and the gullet.

phrases.english: so too here, with most of the two?

steps.triggerLanguage: אי מה להלן ברוב שנים אף כאן ברוב שנים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests whether the comparison in step 1 should be carried further
steps.kashyaTarget: How far the comparison between the עולת העוף and the animal חטאת goes
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the bird learns rules from the animal, it should also learn the rule that most of two סימנים is enough.

steps.title: The head must be fully separated, as it is when burned
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק 'ומלק והקטיר' links pinching to burning. Just as the head and body are burned separately, the pinching must fully separate them.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse says, 'And he shall pinch and burn.' Just as in burning the head is by itself and the body by itself, so too in pinching the head must be by itself and the body by itself.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers the question by pointing to a פסוק. The word for pinching is placed next to the word for burning, so the two acts are compared.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On the מזבח, the head and the body of the bird are burned separately. Since the פסוק puts מליקה right next to הקטרה, the pinching must also fully separate the head from the body. Cutting most of two סימנים is not enough for this offering.

keyTerms.meaning: The verse teaches; introduces a פסוק that settles the question
Pinching: the כהן cuts the bird's neck with his fingernail from the back
Burning the offering on the מזבח

steps.whatToRemember: The עולת העוף is like an animal חטאת in its basic rules, but its head must be completely separated from its body.

phrases.english: The verse says: 'And he shall pinch and burn'
just as in burning, the head is by itself
and the body is by itself,
so too in pinching, the head is by itself
and the body is by itself.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 2 with a פסוק
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits the comparison using a פסוק (היקש between מליקה and הקטרה)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Most of two סימנים might be enough, as with an animal
steps.terutzMaskana: The head must be fully separated from the body, as it is in burning

steps.title: רבי ישמעאל: pinched at the back of the neck, like a bird sin offering
steps.stepSummary: רבי ישמעאל learns from the word 'כמשפט' that the עולת העוף is pinched at the back of the neck, like the חטאת העוף.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ישמעאל says: 'According to the ordinance' means according to the ordinance of the bird sin offering. Just as the bird sin offering is pinched at the back of the neck, so too the bird burnt offering is pinched at the back of the neck.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ישמעאל gives a different source. He compares the עולת העוף to the bird חטאת instead of to an animal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'כמשפט' tells us to do it 'according to the rule' of the חטאת העוף. That offering is pinched ממול ערף, at the back of the neck, so the עולת העוף is pinched there too.

keyTerms.meaning: According to the ordinance (the rule already set out)
A sin offering of a bird
Opposite the nape, at the back of the neck

phrases.english: Rabbi Yishmael says: 'According to the ordinance'
according to the ordinance of the bird sin offering,
just as the bird sin offering is pinched at the back of the neck,
so too the bird burnt offering is pinched at the back of the neck.

steps.triggerLanguage: רבי ישמעאל אומר כמשפט כמשפט חטאת העוף
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second תנא gives a different source for how the עולת העוף is done
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The עולת העוף is pinched at the back of the neck, learned from the חטאת העוף through 'כמשפט'.

steps.title: Should the bird burnt offering also leave one sign uncut?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא asks whether the comparison means the עולת העוף should also keep the head attached by leaving one סימן uncut, like the חטאת העוף.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, then just as there (the bird sin offering) he pinches and does not separate, leaving one סימן, so too here (the bird burnt offering) he should pinch and not separate, leaving one סימן?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא tests רבי ישמעאל's comparison. If the bird עולה is like the bird חטאת, maybe it should also keep its head attached.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the חטאת העוף, the כהן cuts only one סימן and leaves the head attached to the body. The question is whether this detail also carries over to the עולת העוף.

keyTerms.meaning: He does not separate the head from the body
One of the two signs: the windpipe or the gullet

phrases.english: If so, just as there,
he pinches and does not separate, leaving one siman,
phrases.notes: He means only one סימן is cut, so the head stays attached through the other one.

phrases.aramaic: אַף כָּאן מוֹלֵק וְאֵינוֹ מַבְדִּיל בְּסִימָן אֶחָד?
phrases.english: so too here, he pinches and does not separate, leaving one siman?

steps.triggerLanguage: אי מה להלן מולק ואינו מבדיל בסימן אחד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests how far רבי ישמעאל's comparison in step 4 goes
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי ישמעאל's comparison of the עולת העוף to the חטאת העוף
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the bird עולה learns from the bird חטאת, it should also learn the rule that the head stays attached.

steps.title: The word 'and he shall bring it' limits the comparison
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק 'והקריבו' shows that the עולת העוף does not copy the חטאת העוף in leaving the head attached.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse says: 'And he shall bring it.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers with a פסוק. The word 'והקריבו' limits the comparison so that the עולת העוף does not leave a סימן uncut.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The comparison holds for the place of pinching, at the back of the neck. It does not hold for keeping the head attached. In the end, both opinions agree that the עולת העוף's head is fully separated.

keyTerms.meaning: And he shall bring it (near to the מזבח)

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי ישמעאל, the עולת העוף is like the חטאת העוף in being pinched at the back of the neck. But it is not like it in keeping the head attached; the head is fully separated.

phrases.english: The verse says: 'And he shall bring it.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 5 with a פסוק
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits the comparison using a פסוק
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The עולת העוף might leave one סימן uncut, like the חטאת העוף
steps.terutzMaskana: The עולת העוף is not like the חטאת העוף in this detail; its head is separated

steps.title: Another תנא reads 'like the law' as 'like the bird sin offering'
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון explains that the word 'כמשפט' means 'like the law of the חטאת העוף', and begins a comparison: 'just as there...'
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון says: 'According to the law' means 'according to the law of the bird sin offering.' Just as there...
steps.whatsHappening: A new תנא, רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון, gives his own reading of the word 'כמשפט'. He is setting up a comparison between the עולת העוף and the חטאת העוף, and the rest of his comparison comes on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Like רבי ישמעאל in step 4, he says 'כמשפט' points to the rules of the חטאת העוף. The words 'מה להלן' ('just as there') open a comparison: whatever is done 'there', with the חטאת העוף, will also be done 'here', with the עולת העוף. The text stops before telling us which detail he is comparing.

keyTerms.meaning: 'According to the law': a word in the פסוק about the עולת העוף that points to another set of rules
'Just as there': a phrase that opens a comparison to a different case

steps.confusionAlert: Don't assume this is just a repeat of רבי ישמעאל in step 4. It is a different תנא giving his own reading of the same word, and we have to wait for the next lines to see exactly what he learns from it.

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar, son of Rabbi Shimon, says:
"According to the law" means "according to the law of the bird sin offering,"
phrases.notes: This is the same word from the פסוק about the עולת העוף that רבי ישמעאל used back in step 4.

phrases.english: just as there,
phrases.notes: 'There' means the חטאת העוף. The sentence continues in the next part of the text.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר: כַּמִּשְׁפָּט כְּמִשְׁפַּט חַטַּאת הָעוֹף
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the answer in step 6 about רבי ישמעאל's comparison, a different תנא offers his own reading of the same word 'כמשפט'.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The word 'כמשפט' compares the עולת העוף to the law of the חטאת העוף. The details of the comparison begin with 'מה להלן' and continue in the next part of the text.
